article_lead.description: a single prediction for a stated future observation that anchors planning while its uncertainty is assessed separately

new_bank_questions.title: An autoregression two steps ahead
new_bank_questions.body: A stationary AR(1) series has mean 20, coefficient 0.6, innovation variance 9, and latest value 30. Find the conditional-mean forecasts one and two steps ahead and the corresponding forecast-error variances.
new_bank_questions.answer: The forecasts are 20+0.6(30-20)=26 and 20+0.6²(30-20)=23.6. The error variances are 9 and 9(1+0.6²)=12.24. The second forecast has moved toward the mean while uncertainty has increased.

new_bank_questions.title: Which forecast is best under each loss?
new_bank_questions.body: Conditional on today's information, tomorrow's demand is 10 with probability 0.8 and 30 with probability 0.2. Give a forecast minimizing squared error and one minimizing absolute error. Explain why they differ.
new_bank_questions.answer: The conditional mean is 0.8(10)+0.2(30)=14, which minimizes squared error. The conditional median is 10, which minimizes absolute error because 80% of the conditional probability lies there. The two losses penalize misses differently.
